app_js_dependency_audit.note_on_property: app.js reads window.__DASHBOARD_DATA__.property for BOTH the propertyPrice and propertyCredit UI sections (data.js has no separate propertyCredit key).
record_fields_read: url (latest record only, for the source link href)
fields_present_in_data_but_never_read_by: property.preferred (app.js has its own hardcoded `preferred` list per section in its `sections` config -- the data.js copy is unused/vestigial from the UI's perspective)

metrics.<series>.ytd_value / ytd_yoy (retail only -- cumulative year-to-date, plain/latest/published variants: ytd_value, ytd_yoy, latest_ytd_value, latest_ytd_yoy, published_ytd_value, published_ytd_yoy -- all six unread)

metrics.<series>.real_yoy (income only -- inflation-adjusted 实际增长 YoY, present on income_disposable, income_disposable_urban, income_disposable_rural, consumption_expenditure, consumption_expenditure_urban, consumption_expenditure_rural; entirely unread -- the dashboard only ever shows nominal YoY)

chart_mode_logic_keys_expected_by_app_js.version: state.version in {latest, published} -> selects published_month_* vs latest_month_*/month_* fields
chart_mode_logic_keys_expected_by_app_js.mode: state.mode in {value, yoy, trend} -> trend is property-price only, client-computed chained index
chart_mode_logic_keys_expected_by_app_js.retailFrequency: state.retailFrequency in {period, ttm} -> ttm is a client-computed 12-point rolling sum, NOT stored in data
chart_mode_logic_keys_expected_by_app_js.incomeFrequency: state.incomeFrequency in {quarter, ttm, annual} -> ttm is a client-computed 4-point rolling sum over quarterly deltas
chart_mode_logic_keys_expected_by_app_js.incomeScale: state.incomeScale in {percapita, national} -> national multiplies by hardcoded populationWan table in app.js, only when seriesUnit === '元'
chart_mode_logic_keys_expected_by_app_js.propertyCity: state.propertyCity in {overall, core, capitalNewTier, other} -> groups drawn from data.property.cities plus hardcoded city-group lists in app.js
chart_mode_logic_keys_expected_by_app_js.TTM_note: TTM is never a stored flag on a series; it is always a client-side rolling-window computation (window=12 for retail, window=4 for income quarterly points).
chart_mode_logic_keys_expected_by_app_js.revision_variant_note: retail.versioning_note (verbatim): 每个指标保留 latest_*（当前最新版本）与 published_*（发布日期版本）。month_* 字段保留为 latest_* 的兼容别名。

data_oddities.detail: Declared in retail.series with name/group/unit metadata, but no record's metrics.<id> ever carries a non-null value. A migration script that assumes every declared series has >=1 observation will mis-handle these.

21 periods within 1985-01..2026-05 have no record at all in retail.records (not just null metrics -- the whole record is absent). Lines up with years where NBS's Jan/Feb combined-reporting convention was encoded as 'no separate record' rather than 'record with null retail_total' (compare with the flagship_series_internal_nulls finding for retail_total, which is the same convention encoded the other way in later years).

6 periods within 2013-12..2026-03 have no record at all in income.records (not just null metrics -- the whole record is absent). Matches income.coverage_note: 2013-2015 is an annual-only historical-supplement layer, so the intervening quarters genuinely never existed as separate releases.
retail.records exist for these periods but metrics.retail_total has no non-null value.
property.records exist for these periods but metrics.new_home_70_price has no non-null value.

retail.records is not one uniform shape -- 3 distinct key-sets coexist (see records_summary.record_key_signatures for exact counts/keys). A migration script must treat extra provenance fields (release_published_at, release_title, title_period, coverage_note, historical_supplement, quarter) as optional per-record.

income.records is not one uniform shape -- 2 distinct key-sets coexist (see records_summary.record_key_signatures for exact counts/keys). A migration script must treat extra provenance fields (release_published_at, release_title, title_period, coverage_note, historical_supplement, quarter) as optional per-record.
3 of 185 property records have fewer than the declared 70 cities in their nested `cities` dict (likely scrape/source gaps -- see property_city_history_raw.json errors/retryErrors).

retail metrics carry a full YTD family (ytd_value, ytd_yoy, latest_ytd_value, latest_ytd_yoy, published_ytd_value, published_ytd_yoy) and income metrics carry real_yoy (inflation-adjusted growth) on the 6 headline income/consumption series -- app.js reads neither. Live, real data that a redesigned dashboard could surface.
